title: Make check and improve a card stand
goal: I can make from my checked plan and use real checks to improve the work.
success: I can follow the approved cut and join with safe support.
I can stop and compare my work with my plan.
I can log each real adjustment and explain why it helps.
brief: Invented client Sam needs one paper prompt card, 80 mm wide by 60 mm high, upright and readable on a level table. Make a small card stand. It should hold that card for 30 seconds with hands away, fit within a 160 mm by 120 mm overall table area including the channel, let the card lift out by hand and have smooth safe edges. The default body base is 120 mm by 80 mm. These are design targets. Check the actual stand. No heavy object or extra load is used.
dimensions: Default: one suitable thin card body 120 mm wide by 260 mm long. Mark folds across the width at 80, 160 and 240 mm from the same short end. This gives three 80 mm faces and a 20 mm joining tab. Fold a triangle and tape the tab inside the first face at the top seam. Add a 100 mm by 30 mm retaining strip with long folds at 10 and 20 mm from the same long edge. Fold a shallow U channel. Tape its back flange at the bottom of the front sloping face. The shelf projects out and the front stop faces upward toward the card. Leave the stand ends open. Use the actual approved revised plan if it differs.
prepare: Retrieve actual Week 1 designs and Week 2 material choices, cutting lists, step plans and card mock ups. Prepare suitable thin card, rulers, pencils, approved scissors, paper tape, a demonstration sample and one 80 mm by 60 mm paper test card. Try the actual scissors on a sample first. The card must cut and fold safely. Check the clear work area, stable seat, tool condition, support and access needs. Keep prepared pieces available. Reuse and refine an actual Week 2 mock up honestly where suitable. Never relabel it as a new independent build. Count issued tools and arrange safe storage for unfinished work.
safety_before: The adult checks the real plan, tools, card and support before issue.
Use approved scissors only when the adult clears the route. No power tools or heated tools.
If card is too thick or hard to cut, stop. Use safe thinner or prepared card with adult approval.
safety_during: Keep the helping hand outside the cut path. Turn the card and cut away from your body and other people.
Close scissors and put them down before speaking or pausing. Carry closed and pass handle first as shown.
Fold with fingers and a ruler guide. No craft knives, sharp scoring blades, saws or drills in this default route.
Use paper tape for the cold join. Do not wrap tape around skin. No hot glue is used.
safety_after: Put tools down before checking or adjusting. Ask the adult before a further cut.
Return counted tools and clear offcuts as agreed. Stop and tell the adult if a tool is damaged or missing. Do not search through sharp offcuts with bare hands.
Keep unfinished work and its record safe. Test only after adult clearance and when the joint is ready.
fallback: With no card or safe equipment, use the supplied plan for a directed sketch or empty hand rehearsal. Say where you would cut, fold, join and stop to check. Log a proposed change as a proposal. Label the work planning or simulation. Actual cutting, joining, adjustment and testing evidence stay pending unless those actions take place.
alternatives: The default uses suitable thin card, approved scissors, finger folds and paper tape. No glue is needed. A different actual approved design needs its own checked sizes, method and support. Corrugated board may need prepared pieces. Dowel and soft wood are comparison choices from Week 2, not permission for wood cutting here. PVA is used only if the actual plan and adult label checks approve it, with full stated cure before testing. Never invent a cure time. Hot glue is comparison only and is not used. No power tools or heated tools are used.
steps: Find the actual Week 1 design and Week 2 list, material choice, step plan and mock up. Ask the adult to approve the method, tools and support. If a record is missing, agree a new dated plan today and say it is new. Keep actual pupil choices visible.

For the default, mark a body 120 mm by 260 mm and a channel strip 100 mm by 30 mm. Align ruler zero with the chosen edge. Recheck each size. Mark body folds at 80, 160 and 240 mm from the same short end. Mark both long channel folds at 10 and 20 mm from the same long edge. The adult checks before cutting.

The adult shows the agreed scissor grip and a stable position. Keep the helping hand out of the blade path. Cut away from your body and other people. Turn the card to keep the line easy to reach. Close scissors and put them down to stop, speak or change position. Do not force thick card. Use prepared pieces or ask for help.

With tools down, guide each fold with a ruler and press it with fingers. Do not use a sharp scoring edge. Trial fold the three faces into a triangle. The 20 mm tab goes inside the first face at the top seam. Check the triangle sits on its base and the open ends remain clear.

Tape the top seam so the inside tab holds the triangle closed. Fold the retaining strip at both long marks into a shallow U. The 10 mm back flange lies against the bottom of the front sloping face. Tape that flange. The shelf projects out and the front stop faces upward toward the card. Do not flatten the channel or cover its opening with tape.

Tools down. Compare the actual stand with the plan. Ask the adult to clear the joint and test. Put one actual 80 mm by 60 mm paper card in the U channel against the slope. Keep hands away for 30 seconds on a level table. Lift the card out gently. No pushing, shaking, drop test or extra load. Record the real result.

If a check shows a need, keep tools down and ask the adult. Adjust one approved feature, then recheck the same purpose. Log every real change, why it helps and what happened next. A new tape piece, revised fold or channel position must have a real reason. If no change is needed, record the checks and an approved refinement or next step honestly.
stop_checks: Close scissors and put them down. Make the work safe before talking or checking.
Use the actual plan and ruler. Check size, folds, tab and channel. Name one real difference or a check that is met.
Ask the adult if unsure. Agree one safe adjustment linked to the purpose before a tool moves.
Make the approved change with the agreed support. Do not add a new tool or material without approval.
Repeat the relevant check. Record before, change, why, result and support. If the check cannot happen, write pending. Resume only when clear.
model_change: Adult example only: The card slipped during the first agreed test. I saw that the front stop was folded flat. With adult approval I refolded the U so the shelf projected out and the front stop faced up. I then repeated the 30 second test and recorded its actual result. This is a model account, not a pupil result.

hinge.question: The default body should be 120 mm wide. The check range is 118 to 122 mm. Your ruler shows 123 mm. What happens next?
hinge.answer: Stop with tools down. 123 mm is outside 118 to 122 mm. Remeasure from ruler zero. Ask the adult whether a safe trim or a revised part is suitable before joining. Do not cut again without approval.

parallel.question: The channel strip has only one fold at 10 mm. Is it ready to tape on?
parallel.answer: No. The default channel needs two long folds at 10 and 20 mm from the same long edge. Recheck and mark both. Fold the shallow U with a shelf and an upward front stop before joining.

Supported: Use one action at a time with an adult. Point to your actual plan.
Help check the marks or direct adult cutting and joining. Keep the true roles clear.
Use stop and check after each agreed stage.
Explain one actual check and any adjustment. An adult can scribe your words and read them back.
Standard: Use the actual design, cutting list and step plan.
Mark and recheck before the approved cut and join.
Stop and check the stand with the actual paper card when cleared.
Log every real adjustment, its purpose, the recheck result and any support.
Stretch: Complete the core safe build and change log first.
Compare an actual measured result with its target.
Explain how one approved refinement improves stability, card grip or ease of use.
Recheck that feature and state what your actual evidence shows and what remains uncertain.

vocabulary: Turn the checked plan into an actual object.
The place where parts are held together.
A small part that folds in to help a joint.
A shallow U shape that catches the lower edge of the card.
Change one feature after a real check.
Repeat a check after a change.

adaptations.Cognition and Learning: Show one action at a time beside the actual plan. Model the first ruler check then fade that prompt. Use prepared pieces, a fold guide or repeated check words. Record the support and actual pupil role.
adaptations.Communication and Interaction: Offer short instructions and thinking time. Accept speech, pointing, signing or pupil directed adult handling. Read any scribed comment back so the pupil can correct it.
adaptations.SEMH: Use private feedback and choice of calm pause. A pause starts with tools down and work safe. Agree a short return cue. Discuss a difference in the work as information for a change, not a judgement about the pupil.
adaptations.Sensory and Physical: Check handling and seating needs before issue. Offer approved adapted scissors, prepared pieces or pupil directed adult handling. Do not force dense card. A pupil can direct a safe adult action and have that role recorded.
adaptations.Literacy and Numeracy: Keep millimetres as the working unit. Point to ruler zero and the same starting edge for each fold. Offer sentence starts and read the log back. Keep planned and actual numbers in separate fields.
adaptations.EAL: Rehearse in any language. Pair the actual part with cut, fold, tab, shelf and front stop. Check understanding of same edge and tools down before making. Use confirmed scribing where needed.

careers: Construction makers follow plans, choose safe methods and use checks to improve a product. A clear change log helps another person understand why the build changed.

cold_calls.foundation: Point to the tab and the channel. Expected: the inside 20 mm tab and the shallow U that catches the card.
cold_calls.middle: Why do we stop before cutting a 123 mm width again? Expected: it is outside the check range; remeasure and ask the adult to agree a safe correction.
cold_calls.higher: How can a channel change improve the purpose? Expected: a checked shelf and upward front stop can help hold the actual card; only the real recheck shows the result.

misconceptions: A target copied from the plan is an actual measure.
Measure the actual work and record the real value with its unit.
More tape always means a better product.
Use only the tape needed for the approved joint. Keep the channel opening clear and recheck the purpose.
An adjustment can be invented for the log.
Record a real need and change, or honest no change reasoning and a next step.
The making stage means tools can be used alone.
The adult still gives the agreed supervision. Keep true pupil and adult roles in the record.

stages.name: Arrival
stages.title: Our actual plan
pupil: Find your Week 1 design and Week 2 build plan.
Check your material, method and mock up with the adult.
Wait for tools and support to be approved.
stages.teacher: Retrieve the actual records and mock up. Confirm the chosen purpose, sizes, material, joint, tool route and support. If records are missing, agree a new dated recovery plan and label it honestly. Do not invent prior work. Reuse or refine a real Week 2 mock up if suitable. Count tools before issue and check the actual card can be cut and folded safely.
stages.check: Ask what the stand must hold. Expect one actual 80 mm by 60 mm paper card upright on a level table, not a device or heavy load.

stages.name: Starter
stages.title: Read the parts and marks
pupil: Find the body, tab and channel.
Point to the same starting edge for each fold.
Explain the next safe check.
stages.teacher: Use the actual plan or supplied default. The body is 120 by 260 mm; folds at 80, 160 and 240 mm from the same short end. The channel is 100 by 30 mm; both long folds are at 10 and 20 mm from the same long edge. Diagrams are not full size cutting templates.
stages.check: Ask whether a single L fold makes the model channel. No: it needs a shallow U with back flange, shelf and upward front stop.

stages.name: I do
stages.title: A safe cut and cold join
pupil: Watch a checked line and safe scissor action.
See the tab fold inside the triangle.
See the shallow U catch the card edge.
stages.teacher: Demonstrate with suitable thin card and approved scissors. Show the stable position, helping hand clear, cut away from people, turn card and tools down before talking. Use fingers with a ruler guide for folds, not a scoring blade. Dry fit the triangle, tab inside at the top seam, then tape. Show both U folds and tape the back flange to the lower front slope. The shelf projects out and stop faces up. Model one stop and check, then invite the pupil to explain the next action before tools move.
stages.check: Ask pupil to point to a safe helping hand position, inside tab and upward front stop. If unsure, repeat on prepared parts before pupil tool use.

stages.name: We do
stages.title: Make the first checked stage
pupil: Mark and recheck your actual plan.
Use the approved cut or direct adult handling.
Try the folds before taping.
stages.teacher: Guide the first mark and then fade prompts for the next if safe. Check all sizes and fold locations from the same zero edge. Adult clears cutting. Pupils cut using agreed support, or direct an adult. Trial the triangle and U before joining. Keep the demonstration card ready for physical orientation. Record the actual stage; do not rush all cutting into the slot if it is not safe.
stages.check: Check the marked line before each cut and trial fit before tape. A prepared piece is adult preparation, not pupil cutting evidence.

stages.name: We do 2
stages.title: The stop and check hinge
pupil: The target width is 120 mm.
The actual width is 123 mm.
Choose a safe next step and explain why.
stages.teacher: Use the hinge. 123 mm is outside the 118 to 122 mm improvement range. Tools down, remeasure from zero and agree a safe correction with the adult. Parallel check: one long fold at 10 mm does not form the default U channel. It needs folds at 10 and 20 mm from the same long edge. If either check is missed, return to the plan and repeat the trial on prepared parts before making continues. These checks guide improvement, not pupil grades.
stages.check: All pupils can point, speak, sign or direct the safe next action. Recheck understanding before a further cut or join.

stages.name: Independent
stages.title: Make adjust and improve
pupil: Follow the agreed cut and join with support.
Stop and check with the actual paper card when cleared.
Log each real adjustment and why it helps.
stages.teacher: Maintain approved supervision: independent is a timetable stage, not unsupervised tools. Make or refine the actual stand from the approved plan. Clear each joint before testing. Test only one 80 by 60 mm card with hands away for 30 seconds on a level table. Remove it gently. No shaking, pushing, drops or extra load. If needed adjust one approved feature at a time and recheck. Record actual roles and results. For an adhesive alternative wait the full checked label time; testing remains pending if not ready.
stages.check: Observe safe actions, actual joint and checks. Ask what changed and why. Do not invent an adjustment; record real no change reasoning and a next step where appropriate.

stages.name: Review
stages.title: Check the change log
pupil: Put tools down and return them as agreed.
Review each change and its actual result.
Keep unfinished work and the next step clear.
stages.teacher: Collect and count tools before records are reviewed. Adult controls missing or damaged tools. Keep the area clear and do not search sharp offcuts with bare hands. Review the log for before, adjustment, reason linked to purpose, recheck result and support/date. Confirm any no change account from real checks. Store actual work and records together.
stages.check: A change entry needs an actual check and real reason. A proposed adjustment is labelled proposed; an unperformed recheck stays pending.

stages.name: Exit
stages.title: My true making record
pupil: I made or directed ___.
I changed ___ because ___ / my check showed no change was needed.
My next safe step is ___.
stages.teacher: Retain the actual item or model with dated design and plan references, pupil words, roles, checks, each real change and next step. Let the pupil correct scribed words. A materials free rehearsal stays simulation. Weekly evidence can support the unit award only when it matches actual observed actions and criteria.
stages.check: The record distinguishes pupil making, adult making, mock up, simulation and unfinished practical work. Do not confirm the unit award from this lesson alone.
